gadgets.sink: prototype pollution -> arbitrary file write, via the `output` option
gadgets.payload: Object.prototype.output = "/app/views/<a view no request has rendered yet>.html"; Object.prototype.parse_response = false
gadgets.effect: needle reads `output` with a bare `options.output` and every other option through a get_option() that falls through to the prototype, so when the caller passes an object LITERAL (needle.get(url, {compressed:true, follow_max:0}, cb)) every option is prototype-reachable. With `output` set, a 200 response body is written to that path: the SSRF becomes an arbitrary file write, and a template directory turns it into RCE.
gadgets.precondition: the options bag handed to needle is a plain object literal (not Object.create(null)), the response is HTTP 200 (needle only writes on 200), and something later reads the written path
gadgets.trap: MANDATORY companion: pollute parse_response:false too. At the default parse_response:'all' needle parses a JSON response and then calls file.write(chunk) on the parsed OBJECT -> ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE from node:internal/streams/writable. If the calling handler has no try/catch that escapes as an unhandled rejection and kills the process. Polluting only `output` looks fine against an HTML response and crashes the app against a JSON one.

gadgets.sink: prototype pollution -> request control, via cookies / headers / proxy
gadgets.effect: adds a Cookie header (cookies.write), arbitrary headers, or redirects the whole request to another host:port with the original URI as the request-line path. Lets the polluted client authenticate to the app it is being pointed at.
gadgets.trap: follow_max cannot be raised this way when the caller passes it explicitly: get_option() prefers the caller's OWN property over the prototype, so an own follow_max:0 stays 0
